transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-05 09:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (CSM), Diego Alvarez (SE) --- Asha Reddy (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Mia Chen (PM)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/rec/ff-20270805-ngt-001 (not included)

Summary: quick alignment on Dedicated runtime provisioning and SLA expectations; initial perf plan agreed, networking/VPC steps reviewed.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Mills: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um just quick intros then we'll jump into the provisioning checklist.
[00:09] Asha Reddy: Thanks Jordan, hi all, Asha here — we run ML infra at NeptuneGrid, we're looking to roll Redwood for inference across our customer-facing API by Q4.
[00:18] Priya Kapoor: Great — I'm Priya, your CSM, I'll be handling the onboarding runway and playbooks. Diego from SE will handle the benchmarks and runtime questions.
[00:28] Diego Alvarez: Hi — Diego Alvarez, Solutions Eng. I'll be your point on perf, kernels, batching and the quantization profile stuff.
[00:35] Liam O'Connor: Liam — infra. we'll own VPC peering, firewall, and certs. quick note: our security team wants SOC2 docs and an audit of logging before we open anything.
[00:45] Jordan Mills: Noted — we have the SOC2 and ISO docs in the security pack, we'll share that. Also we should align on the SLA targets you mentioned in the RFP.
[00:53] Mia Chen: For product the main KPI is p95 latency under 300ms for single-turn text generation at our typical batch size, and sustained throughput of about 6k tokens/sec per region.
[01:05] Diego Alvarez: Okay quick callout — p95 300ms depends a lot on sequence length and batching. For 256 token prompts that might be tight on a shared hosted tier; Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching you'll have a lot more headroom.
[01:20] Asha Reddy: We're planning dedicated pools — we want predictable latency during peak shopping hours. Cost is a concern but predictability and DR are higher priority.
[01:30] Jordan Mills: That maps well to Redwood Dedicated — predictable GPU pools, can configure burst policies. We'll show two capacity sizing options in the follow-up pricing.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: On networking: we'll need the exact egress CIDRs and the service endpoint IP ranges; also do you support Private Deployments with tenant isolation?
[01:49] Priya Kapoor: Yes — Redwood Private (VPC) is an option, and Dedicated can be VPC-peered. We'll send the network checklist. small aside — sometimes the doc tooling calls it Redwood Dedicate in auto notes, ignore the typo.
[02:04] Diego Alvarez: For the benchmark plan, we'd like a representative prompt set; Asha if you can send the production-ish prompts we'll run a 2-hour soak at peak qps and a 10k-rps spike test in staging.
[02:16] Asha Reddy: We can do that — we'll redact PII and send a 500-sample corpus.
[02:22] Jordan Mills: Cool. Diego, can you confirm what metrics you'll provide from the bench?
[02:27] Diego Alvarez: We'll provide p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU utilization, memory footprints, KV cache hit rates, and a token-cost estimate. Also a comparison between FP16 and int8 quantized paths.
[02:40] Mia Chen: On rollouts — we need canary deploys and an automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency spikes. Do you have automatic fallback policies?
[02:48] Diego Alvarez: Yes we have routing policies — latency- and cost-based. We can configure a canary to 5% traffic, auto rollback if error rate > X or latency > threshold. Note: we need compatibility between model variants for seamless fallback.
[03:04] Liam O'Connor: What about logs and audit? our compliance team requires request-level audit logs for 30 days and S3 export.
[03:12] Priya Kapoor: We support audit logs, export to your S3, and access via the Redwood Console. For long-retention we have add-on packages for 90/365 days.
[03:22] Asha Reddy: Great. Also encryption — KMS integration for key management?
[03:26] Jordan Mills: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — we'll include the KMS integration doc in the security pack.
[03:34] Mia Chen: Timeline question: assuming we sign a reserved capacity contract, how long to prod?
[03:40] Priya Kapoor: Typical ramp-to-prod for Dedicated is 6-8 weeks after access and staging readiness — network, test corpus, and service account exchange are usually the gating items.
[03:51] Liam O'Connor: That aligns. We'll target staging access this week to keep momentum.
[03:56] Diego Alvarez: Technical note on inference: if you have long-context dialogs we recommend the KV cache enabled with prefix caching; that reduces token cost but needs a model variant compiled with cache-friendly kernels. We'll discuss compile options in the deep dive.
[04:12] Asha Reddy: One of our concerns — model regressions after upgrades. Is there a rollback and eval hook?
[04:17] Diego Alvarez: Yes — rollouts are tied to evals. We can run your prompt set against the new version and gate rollout on quality metrics. We'll include the eval harness in the SE deep dive.
[04:28] Jordan Mills: Okay, quickly let's go through immediate checklist so we have clear owners. Prio 1: network/CIDR peering, Prio 2: sample prompts, Prio 3: benchmark harness, Prio 4: security docs.
[04:41] Asha Reddy: We'll handle sample prompts and security contact. Liam will do networking.
[04:46] Liam O'Connor: Yes I'll open the firewall and share the CIDR ranges by Friday. One question: do you require a site-to-site VPN or is VPC peering enough?
[04:56] Priya Kapoor: VPC peering is sufficient for Dedicated, but for on-prem air-gapped we'd use the private package. We'll add a note in the checklist about VPN options.
[05:06] Mia Chen: On cost: can you give a ballpark for a 24/7 Dedicated pool that handles our target throughput?
[05:12] Jordan Mills: I'll follow up with two options — a baseline reserved pool and a burst-enabled pool. I'll send that by EOD Friday.
[05:19] Diego Alvarez: For the bench I'll propose two configs: 1) Balanced: FP16, medium batch, 2) Cost-savvy: int8 quant + more aggressive batching. We'll measure both.
[05:31] Asha Reddy: Sounds good. Any blockers for us to start the staging perf test?
[05:35] Priya Kapoor: We need the prompts and CIDR ranges; Diego also needs an IAM/service-account with token.
[05:42] Liam O'Connor: We'll provision a service-account and share credentials via your secure intake flow.
[05:48] Jordan Mills: Great. Let's recap next steps and owners — then we'll open the calendar for the technical deep dive.
[05:54] (Brief pause)
[06:00] Jordan Mills: Recap: Priya send runbook & network checklist (due 8/6), Diego prepare benchmark harness (due 8/9), NeptuneGrid to share prompts and CIDR (due 8/6-8/8), Jordan send pricing options (due 8/7).
[06:20] Mia Chen: One last Q: is there a staging cost or credits for testing?
[06:25] Jordan Mills: We usually provide limited staging credits for benchmark runs; I'll include that in the follow-up note.
[06:32] Asha Reddy: Perfect. Thanks all.
[06:36] Jordan Mills: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes and docs. Talk soon.
[06:40] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker overlap, occasional auto-transcription errors (e.g., Redwood Dedicate), proper nouns sometimes garbled.

Referenced artifacts: onboarding_runbook_v1.pdf (shared), network_cidr_template.csv (shared), initial_bench_plan.xlsx (to be shared by Diego).
